newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to assist regional gas field development.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to assist regional gas field development.

text.p: South African was committed to the development of regional gas-based industries and was finalising a new gas law, Minerals and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said on Wednesday.
Addressing a news briefing, he said he expected a gas trade agreement to be concluded with Mozambique early next year and one with Namibia soon afterwards.
Mozambique and Namibia have huge offshore gas fields but have been unable to develop them because of a lack of anchor clients in South Africa to make commercial exploitation viable.

"We are developing a gas policy and gas law," Maduna said. "The gas industry in the whole of the sub-region of Southern Africa is developing because there is a lot of natural gas and a lot of coal-bed methane that we want to tap."
He said South Africa had already concluded negotiations on a draft gas trade agreement with Mozambique.
Maduna said details were being circulated to various government departments and should be finalised next year.
"We think that we...together with (other regional) member states, should begin to use those resources," he said.
"Gas, needless to say, is going to be competing with our coal, which we have in abundance and we will have to weigh all sorts of options."
Gas was environmentally cleaner than coal and if it could be used in a cost effective way, government would begin to "nudge" the country and economy in that direction, Maduna said.

"It is obvious that there will never be movement unless South Africa becomes available as a market so we are as government committed to ensuring that those resources are used for the development, not just of South Africa, but of the whole sub-region."
He would not be drawn on whether a power station or developments at Saldanha Bay would be the anchor clients for the Kudu field.

"Those are questions of detail. It is enough for us to say from the policy perspective position this is what we have committed ourselves to do and those basic technical decisions will be taken by (others)," he said.
He said Sasol had shown interest in using the gas and any downstream development would probably be undertaken through a combination of public and private investment.
